candidates.comment: A general association relation between two products or services that have some unspecified connection. Also called associated with, connected to, linked to, relevant to. Examples: A smartphone isRelatedTo 'a smart watch'. A car service isRelatedTo 'car insurance'. A book isRelatedTo 'a movie adaptation'. Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: relatedStructure
candidates.comment: A related structure relation between an anatomical system and structures that connect to or are associated with it, but are not part of the system itself. Also called associated structure, connected structure. Examples: "The circulatory system has a related structure 'the heart'.", "The nervous system has a related structure 'the brain'.", "The digestive system has a related structure 'the liver'."

candidates.label: relatedTo
candidates.comment: A familial relation between two people, representing a generic family connection. Also called family member, kin, relative. Examples: "John is related to 'Jane'.", "Mary is related to 'Tom'.", "Aunt Sally is related to 'Nephew Bob'."

candidates.label: relatedLink
candidates.comment: A related link relation between a web page and a URL pointing to another relevant web page. Also called external link, associated link, further reading. Examples: "A news article has a related link to 'the source report'.", "A product page has a related link to 'customer reviews'.", "A blog post has a related link to 'a previous article'."

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: connectedTo
candidates.comment: A connection relation between an anatomical structure and other anatomical structures it is connected to. Also called "linked to", "adjoins", "connects with". Examples: "Femur anatomical structure connectedTo Tibia", "Brain anatomical structure connectedTo Spinal cord".

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: affiliation
candidates.comment: An affiliation relation between a person and an organization they are associated with. Also called associated with, member of, works for, belongs to. Examples: "A professor's affiliation is 'Harvard University'.", "A player's affiliation is 'Local Soccer Club'." Distinct from alumniOf, which specifies a past association with an educational organization.

candidates.label: relatedCondition
candidates.comment: A related condition relation between an anatomical structure or system and a medical condition associated with it. Also called associated condition, condition of, affects condition. Examples: "The knee joint has a related condition 'arthritis'.", "The respiratory system has a related condition 'asthma'.", "The skin has a related condition 'eczema'."

candidates.label: associatedDisease
candidates.comment: A medical condition or URL representing a disease linked to a biochemical entity. Also called: related disease, disease connection, disease association. Examples: "BioChemEntity 'Insulin' associatedDisease 'Diabetes'", "BioChemEntity 'Gene X' associatedDisease 'Cancer'", "BioChemEntity 'Drug Y' associatedDisease 'Hypertension'."

candidates.label: skills
candidates.comment: The competencies, knowledge, or abilities possessed by a person or organization, or required for a job or occupation. Also called competencies, abilities, qualifications, expertise. Examples: `Job Posting: Software Engineer` skills `"Python, Java, SQL"`, `Person: Jane Doe` skills `"Project Management, Public Speaking"`, `Occupation: Doctor` skills `"Diagnosis, Patient Care"`. Distinct from `qualifications`, which are formal requirements.

candidates.label: teaches
candidates.comment: An educational relation between a creative work, education event, or learning resource and the competency or learning outcome it is designed to teach. Also called "educates on", "imparts knowledge of", "instructs in", "covers topic". Examples: "The course teaches 'Algebra'", "The learning resource teaches problem-solving skills", "This event teaches advanced programming concepts."

candidates.label: competencyRequired
candidates.comment: A requirement relation for an educational credential or learning resource, specifying the knowledge, skill, or ability needed. Also called "required skill", "prerequisite competency", "learning outcome". Examples: "Certification competencyRequired 'Problem-solving skills'", "Course learning resource competencyRequired 'Basic algebra'".

candidates.label: proficiencyLevel
candidates.comment: A proficiency level relation between a technical article and the skill level required to understand its content. Also called skill level, required expertise, target audience level. Examples: "A Python tutorial has a proficiency level of 'Beginner'.", "A deep learning research paper has a proficiency level of 'Expert'.", "A guide to advanced calculus has a proficiency level of 'Intermediate'."

candidates.label: qualifications
candidates.comment: A qualification relation between a job posting or occupation and the specific credentials or skills required. Also called required skills, job requirements, eligibility criteria. Examples: "A software engineer job posting requires qualifications like a 'Bachelor's degree in Computer Science'.", "A doctor's occupation requires qualifications like 'Medical License'.", "A project manager role requires qualifications like 'PMP certification'."

candidates.label: knowsAbout
candidates.comment: A knowledge domain relation between an organization or person and a topic or entity they possess knowledge about. Also called knowledgeable about, familiar with topic, understands, has expertise in (without implying skill level). Examples: A person knowsAbout 'artificial intelligence'. An organization knowsAbout 'renewable energy policy'. A researcher knowsAbout 'quantum physics'. Distinct from hasOccupation or alumniOf, which are about formal roles or education, not general knowledge.

candidates.label: material
candidates.comment: A material composition relation between a creative work or product and the material it is made from. Also called: made of, composed of, constructed from. Examples: "Wooden Chair material Wood", "Wool Sweater material Wool", "Paper Book material Paper".

candidates.label: assesses
candidates.comment: A relation between a creative work, education event, or learning resource and the competency or learning outcome it is intended to evaluate. Also called: evaluates, measures, tests, gauges. Examples: "LearningResource 'Quiz' assesses 'Understanding of Algebra'", "EducationEvent 'Exam' assesses 'Problem-solving skills'", "CreativeWork 'Rubric' assesses 'Writing proficiency'."

candidates.label: learningResourceType
candidates.comment: A learning resource classification relation between a creative work or learning resource and its predominant type or format. Also called resource format, learning material type, educational resource kind. Examples: A learning resource has a learningResourceType of 'presentation'. A creative work has a learningResourceType of 'handout'. An online course module has a learningResourceType of 'interactive simulation'. Distinct from resourceType, which is a more general property for any resource.

candidates.label: educationalUse
candidates.comment: An educational use relation between a creative work or learning resource and its purpose in an educational context. Also called "learning purpose", "pedagogical use", "instructional application". Examples: "Worksheet educationalUse 'Assignment'", "Video educationalUse 'Group work'", "Simulation educationalUse 'Experiment'".

candidates.label: artMedium
candidates.comment: A material or technique used in the creation of a visual artwork. Also called: artistic medium, material used, technique. Examples: "VisualArtwork 'Portrait' artMedium 'Oil on canvas'", "VisualArtwork 'Sketch' artMedium 'Pencil'", "VisualArtwork 'Digital Art' artMedium 'Digital'". Distinct from artform, which describes the general category of art.

candidates.label: ccRecipient
candidates.comment: A recipient relation for a message, indicating a contact point, organization, or person who is copied on it. Also called "carbon copy recipient", "copied to", "CC'd party". Examples: "Email message ccRecipient John Doe", "Internal memo message ccRecipient HR Department".

candidates.label: surface
candidates.comment: An identification of the material used as the surface for a visual artwork. Also called "artwork medium", "painting surface", "material base", "substrate". Examples: "The painting has surface canvas", "The drawing's surface is paper", "This artwork uses a wood surface."

candidates.label: artist
candidates.comment: A person who is the primary creator of a comic issue, comic story, or visual artwork, especially in non-line art mediums. Also called: creator, illustrator, visual creator. Examples: "VisualArtwork 'Starry Night' artist 'Vincent van Gogh'", "ComicIssue 'Issue #1' artist 'Frank Miller'", "ComicStory 'Origin Story' artist 'Alex Ross'". Distinct from author, which is a more general term for the creator of content, often textual.

candidates.label: dateCreated
candidates.comment: A temporal origin relation between a creative work or data feed item and the date it was created or added. Also called: creation date, date of origin, initial date. Examples: "Painting" date created "1889-05-01", "Blog Post" date created "2023-03-15T10:00:00Z", "Data Feed Entry" date created "2023-01-01". Distinct from datePublished, which is the date of first public release.

candidates.label: publishedOn
candidates.comment: A broadcast publication relation between a publication event and the broadcast service on which it was published. Also called aired on, broadcast via, released on service. Examples: "A TV show's publication event was published on 'BBC One'.", "A radio program's publication event was published on 'NPR'.", "A news segment's publication event was published on 'CNN'."

candidates.label: produces
candidates.comment: An outcome relation between a service and the tangible thing it generates or provides. Also called generates, yields, creates, provides. Examples: A government service produces a 'passport'. A licensing service produces a 'permit'. A printing service produces 'documents'.

candidates.label: issuedThrough
candidates.comment: A service channel relation between a permit and the specific service used to obtain it. Also called obtained via, granted through, service channel. Examples: A building permit was issuedThrough 'Online Permit Application System'. A fishing license was issuedThrough 'State Wildlife Service'. A visa was issuedThrough 'Consular Services Department'. Distinct from issuedBy, which is the organization, not the service.

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: creator
candidates.comment: An authorship relation between a creative work or user comment and the person or organization responsible for its creation. Also called: author, originator, producer, made by. Examples: "Novel" creator "Jane Doe", "Software" creator "Acme Corp.", "Blog Post" creator "John Smith", "User Review" creator "Anonymous User". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which is about legal ownership.

candidates.label: free
candidates.comment: A free relation indicating whether a publication event, item, or place is accessible without cost. Also called: no charge, complimentary, gratis. Examples: "Online Article Publication" free "true", "Concert Event" free "false", "Public Park Access" free "true".

candidates.label: isAccessibleForFree
candidates.comment: An access cost relation indicating whether a creative work, event, or place can be accessed without charge. Also called free access, no charge, complimentary access, free of cost. Examples: A public park has isAccessibleForFree set to 'true'. An online article has isAccessibleForFree set to 'true'. A concert has isAccessibleForFree set to 'false'.

candidates.label: ineligibleRegion
candidates.comment: A geographical exclusion relation between an action access specification, delivery charge specification, demand, media object, or offer, and the region where it is not valid or available. Also called restricted region, excluded region, unavailable in, not valid in. Examples: An offer has an ineligibleRegion of 'Alaska'. A delivery charge specification has an ineligibleRegion of 'Hawaii'. A media object has an ineligibleRegion of 'EU'. Distinct from eligibleRegion, which specifies where something *is* valid or available.

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: nonEqual
candidates.comment: A qualitative value that is not equal to another qualitative value. Also called not equivalent to, different from, unequal to. Examples: "Value A nonEqual 'Value B'", "Color Red nonEqual 'Color Blue'", "Size Small nonEqual 'Size Large'". Distinct from equal, which indicates equivalence.

candidates.label: supply
candidates.comment: A resource relation between a how-to guide or direction and a consumable supply required for its execution. Also called "required supply", "consumable item", "material needed", "ingredient". Examples: "The recipe has supply flour", "The how-to direction requires supply glue", "This guide lists several supply items.". Distinct from tool, which refers to a non-consumable instrument.

candidates.label: countriesNotSupported
candidates.comment: A geographical restriction relation between a software application and the countries where it is not supported. Also called: unsupported regions, restricted countries, unavailable in. Examples: "App X" countries not supported "Cuba", "Software Y" countries not supported "Iran, North Korea", "Game Z" countries not supported "Syria". Distinct from countriesSupported, which lists where the application is supported.

candidates.label: doesNotShip
candidates.comment: A does not ship relation between offer shipping details, shipping conditions, or shipping rate settings and a boolean value indicating when shipping to a particular destination is unavailable. Also called "shipping unavailable", "no shipping to", "delivery excluded". Examples: "Offer shipping details doesNotShip 'true' for Alaska", "Shipping conditions doesNotShip 'true' for international orders", "Shipping rate settings doesNotShip 'true' for PO boxes".

candidates.label: owner
candidates.comment: A person or organization that owns a thing. Also called proprietor, possessor, title holder. Examples: "Car owner 'John Doe'", "Company owner 'Acme Corp'", "House owner 'Smith Family Trust'". Distinct from creator, who made the thing.

candidates.label: requiredQuantity
candidates.comment: A required quantity relation between a how-to item and the amount of that item needed. Also called quantity needed, amount required. Examples: "A how-to item 'sugar' has a required quantity '1 cup'.", "A crafting project needs a required quantity '5 sheets of paper'.", "A recipe step specifies a required quantity '2 eggs'."

candidates.label: status
candidates.comment: An indication of the current state or status of a medical condition, procedure, or study. Also called "current state", "condition status", "study progress", "procedure status". Examples: "The medical study has status Recruiting", "The patient's condition status is stable", "The procedure's status is completed."

candidates.label: orderStatus
candidates.comment: The current status of an entire order. Also called order state, transaction status, fulfillment state. Examples: "Order 123 orderStatus 'OrderProcessing'", "Order 456 orderStatus 'OrderDelivered'", "Order 789 orderStatus 'OrderCancelled'". Distinct from orderItemStatus, which is for individual items within an order.

candidates.label: eventStatus
candidates.comment: An event status relation between an event and its current status type. Also called "event condition", "status of event", "event state". Examples: "Event 'Concert' eventStatus 'EventCancelled'", "Event 'Meeting' eventStatus 'EventScheduled'", "Event 'Festival' eventStatus 'EventRescheduled'".

candidates.label: actionStatus
candidates.comment: An action status relation between an action and its current disposition or state. Also called action state, status of action, disposition. Examples: "A 'purchase' action's action status is 'CompletedActionStatus'.", "A 'shipment' action's action status is 'PotentialActionStatus'."

candidates.label: serverStatus
candidates.comment: The current operational status of a game server. Also called server state, game server condition, operational status. Examples: `Game Server A` serverStatus `Online`, `Game Server B` serverStatus `Offline`, `Game Server C` serverStatus `Maintenance`.

candidates.label: itemCondition
candidates.comment: A product state relation indicating the physical condition of a product or service, or the condition required for returns. Also called product state, condition of item, quality status, return condition. Examples: An offer has an itemCondition of 'NewCondition'. A product has an itemCondition of 'UsedCondition'. A return policy specifies itemCondition 'SellerRefurbished'.

candidates.label: paymentStatus
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the current payment status of an invoice. Also called invoice status, payment condition, settlement status. Examples: An invoice has a payment status of 'PaymentComplete'. An invoice has a payment status of 'PaymentDue'. An invoice has a payment status of 'PaymentFailed'.

candidates.label: orderItemStatus
candidates.comment: The current status of an order item. Also called item status, line item status, fulfillment status. Examples: "OrderItem A orderItemStatus 'OrderProcessing'", "OrderItem B orderItemStatus 'OrderShipped'", "OrderItem C orderItemStatus 'OrderDelivered'". Distinct from orderStatus, which is for the entire order.

candidates.label: reservationStatus
candidates.comment: A reservation status relation between a reservation and its current state, such as confirmed or cancelled. Also called booking status, status of reservation. Examples: "A flight reservation has a reservation status 'Confirmed'.", "A hotel booking has a reservation status 'Pending'.", "A restaurant reservation has a reservation status 'Cancelled'."

candidates.label: availability
candidates.comment: The current status of an item's availability for demand or offer. Also called: stock status, item status, product availability. Examples: "Offer 'Product X' availability 'InStock'", "Demand 'Service Y' availability 'OutOfStock'", "Offer 'Limited Edition' availability 'PreOrder'."

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: creditedTo
candidates.comment: An attribution relation between a music release and the group or artist it is credited to, if different from the primary artist. Also called: attributed to, release credit, presented by. Examples: "Album 'Red and Blue'" credited to "Stefani Germanotta Band", "Single 'X'" credited to "The Session Musicians", "Soundtrack" credited to "Various Artists".

candidates.label: error
candidates.comment: An error relation between a failed action and the thing providing more information on the cause of the failure. Also called "failure cause", "problem details", "issue description". Examples: "Action 'Payment' error 'Insufficient Funds'", "Action 'Login' error 'Invalid Credentials'", "Action 'File Upload' error 'File Too Large'". Distinct from errorCode, which is a specific code for the error.

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: infectiousAgent
candidates.comment: A causative agent relation between an infectious disease and the specific microorganism or pathogen that causes it. Also called causative organism, pathogen, disease agent, etiological agent. Examples: Influenza has an infectiousAgent of 'Influenza virus'. Tuberculosis has an infectiousAgent of 'Mycobacterium tuberculosis'. Malaria has an infectiousAgent of 'Plasmodium falciparum'. Distinct from infectiousAgentClass, which specifies the *type* of agent (e.g., bacteria, virus).

candidates.label: seriousAdverseOutcome
candidates.comment: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.

candidates.label: affectedBy
candidates.comment: An affected by relation between a medical test and the drugs that can influence its results. Also called influenced by, impacted by, drug interaction. Examples: "A blood test's results are affected by 'anticoagulants'.", "The diagnostic test is affected by 'caffeine'."

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: spatialCoverage
candidates.comment: A geographic focus relation between a creative work and the place(s) that are the primary subject or focus of its content. Also called "geographic scope", "covered area", "location focus", "content location". Examples: "A weather dataset has spatialCoverage New York State", "The historical map's spatialCoverage is ancient Rome", "This research paper's spatialCoverage is the Arctic region.". Distinct from spatial, which is a more general spatial association when the specific focus is not known.

candidates.label: aspect
candidates.comment: A specific area or topic of medical practice considered on a medical webpage. Also called: medical topic, health aspect, clinical focus. Examples: "MedicalWebPage 'Diabetes' aspect 'diagnosis'", "MedicalWebPage 'Flu' aspect 'treatment'", "MedicalWebPage 'Cancer' aspect 'prognosis'."

candidates.label: studySubject
candidates.comment: An investigative relation between a medical study and the medical entity (condition, therapy, drug, etc.) that is being investigated. Also called "subject of investigation", "research focus", "entity studied", "trial subject". Examples: "The medical study has studySubject a new drug", "The clinical trial's studySubject is a specific medical condition", "This study investigates a studySubject therapy."

candidates.label: guidelineSubject
candidates.comment: A guideline subject relation between a medical guideline and the medical conditions, treatments, or other entities it addresses. Also called: guideline topic, subject matter, focus. Examples: "AHA Guideline for Hypertension" guideline subject "Hypertension", "NICE Guideline for Diabetes" guideline subject "Type 2 Diabetes", "WHO COVID-19 Guidelines" guideline subject "COVID-19". Distinct from guideline, which is the guideline itself.

candidates.label: hasHealthAspect
candidates.comment: A health aspect relation between health topic content and the specific health aspect it addresses. Also called content aspect, topic aspect, health focus. Examples: "Health topic content has a health aspect of 'treatment'.", "The article has a health aspect of 'self-care'.", "This content addresses a health aspect of 'overview'."

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: reviewAspect
candidates.comment: The specific part, feature, or facet of an item that a review or rating pertains to. Also called review focus, aspect reviewed, rating dimension. Examples: `Restaurant Review` reviewAspect `"Service Quality"`, `Product Rating` reviewAspect `"Battery Life"`, `Movie Review` reviewAspect `"Acting Performance"`.

candidates.label: specialty
candidates.comment: A categorization of a webpage's content by its domain specialty. Also called "domain expertise", "content area", "subject specialty", "field of study". Examples: "This medical webpage has specialty Cardiology", "The research paper's specialty is Artificial Intelligence", "The blog post's specialty is Vegan Cooking."

candidates.label: missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy
candidates.comment: A mission coverage priorities policy relation between a news media organization and a creative work or URL stating its coverage priorities or public agenda. Also called: editorial policy, coverage guidelines, journalistic priorities. Examples: "News Outlet missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy 'Focus on local news and investigative journalism'", "Broadcaster missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy 'Public Service Mandate'", "Digital Publisher missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy 'Transparency and Accuracy Statement'".

candidates.label: isSimilarTo
candidates.comment: A functional resemblance relation between two products or services that share similar characteristics or purposes. Also called similar to, comparable to, analogous to, like. Examples: Product A isSimilarTo 'Product B' (a competitor's product). Service X isSimilarTo 'Service Y' (an alternative service). A specific brand of coffee isSimilarTo 'another brand of coffee'. Distinct from isRelatedTo, which is a more general association without implying functional similarity.

candidates.label: greaterOrEqual
candidates.comment: A greater or equal relation indicating that one qualitative value is superior to or the same as another. Also called: is greater than or equal to, at least, no less than. Examples: "High" greater or equal "Medium", "Good" greater or equal "Good", "Large" greater or equal "Medium". Distinct from greater, which does not include equality.

candidates.label: differentialDiagnosis
candidates.comment: A diagnostic comparison relation between a medical condition and one of a set of closely-related or competing diagnoses. Also called: competing diagnosis, alternative diagnosis, diagnostic possibilities. Examples: "Headache" differential diagnosis "Migraine", "Chest Pain" differential diagnosis "Heartburn", "Fever" differential diagnosis "Influenza". Distinct from diagnosis, which is the final identified condition.

candidates.label: lesserOrEqual
candidates.comment: A lesser or equal ordering relation between two qualitative values, indicating that the subject value is smaller than or equal to the object value. Also called: is less than or equal to, is at most, does not exceed. Examples: "Low lesserOrEqual Medium", "Small lesserOrEqual Small", "Cold lesserOrEqual Cold". Distinct from lesser, which strictly indicates a smaller value.

candidates.label: lesser
candidates.comment: A lesser ordering relation between two qualitative values, indicating that the subject value is smaller than the object value. Also called: is less than, is smaller than, falls below. Examples: "Low lesser Medium", "Small lesser Large", "Cold lesser Warm". Distinct from lesserOrEqual, which includes equality.

candidates.label: greater
candidates.comment: A greater relation indicating that one qualitative value is superior or larger than another. Also called: is greater than, exceeds, is more than. Examples: "High" greater "Medium", "Excellent" greater "Good", "Large" greater "Small". Distinct from greaterOrEqual, which includes equality.

candidates.label: nonEqual
candidates.comment: A qualitative value that is not equal to another qualitative value. Also called not equivalent to, different from, unequal to. Examples: "Value A nonEqual 'Value B'", "Color Red nonEqual 'Color Blue'", "Size Small nonEqual 'Size Large'". Distinct from equal, which indicates equivalence.

candidates.label: image
candidates.comment: An image relation between any thing and a visual representation of it. Also called picture, photo, visual. Examples: "A product has an image of its front view.", "A person has an image as a profile picture.", "This thing has an image URL."

candidates.label: equal
candidates.comment: An equality relation between two qualitative values, indicating that the subject qualitative value is considered equal to the object qualitative value within a specific ordering context. Also called "is equivalent to", "is the same as", "matches". Examples: "Qualitative value 'Satisfactory' equal 'Acceptable'", "Qualitative value 'Medium' equal 'Average'", "Qualitative value 'High' equal 'Very Good'".

candidates.label: distinguishingSign
candidates.comment: A distinguishing sign relation between a differential diagnosis element and a medical sign or symptom that helps differentiate it from other diagnoses. Also called "differential symptom", "diagnostic indicator", "key symptom". Examples: "DDx element 'Appendicitis' distinguishingSign 'Right lower quadrant pain'", "DDx element 'Flu' distinguishingSign 'Sudden onset'", "DDx element 'Migraine' distinguishingSign 'Aura'".
